markdown_report:
At 10% research progress, prioritize a small diagnostic improvement that tests hypotheses before spending the training budget.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics has a 14.95% sampled training misranking rate versus 3.03% for Movies_and_TV; this motivates category-specific investigation without establishing validation performance. (2) Deletions compact positions, mixing content and positional effects. (3) Feedback distinguishes relatedness from usefulness, but histories cannot establish purpose, compatibility, or dislike.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Recency sensitivity need not be harmful [1,2]. (2) Position-preserving substitutions have precedent [5], limiting originality. (3) Sampled and catalog rankings can disagree [3]. (4) Personalized judgments require uncertainty [4]; ID-only SASRec cannot directly use title words [6]. Text-matched substitutions therefore measure item-identity sensitivity, not lexical causation.

These insights define three directions: isolate sequence mechanisms; audit ranking across candidate sets; and attach evidence and uncertainty to semantic judgments.

| Direction | Existing method | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sequence mechanisms | Compacted deletions | Same-donor, position-preserving replacements | Synthetic histories and residual imbalance |
| Ranking reliability | Sampled training margins | Fixed catalog ranks and simple behavioral controls | Sensitivity is not accuracy |
| Semantic evidence | Qualitative feedback | Text-supported hypotheses with abstention | Intent remains unobserved |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Matched replacement probe — 4/7/5.** Originality: useful paired controls, but substitution precedent exists. Potential: exposes confounds, but cannot establish intent. Difficulty: scoring hooks exist, but joint matching and donor controls require care [1,2,5].
- **Candidate-set disagreement audit — 4/7/4.** Originality: useful stratification, but established analysis. Potential: reveals misleading margins, but may not predict gains. Difficulty: straightforward scoring, substantial catalog cost [3].
- **Evidence-backed unresolved-case rubric — 5/6/6.** Originality: adapts selective judgment, largely annotation. Potential: improves interpretation, needs independent labels. Difficulty: simple schema, costly validation [4].
- **Behavioral control ladder — 3/8/3.** Originality: established baselines, useful combination. Potential: tests cheaper explanations, without establishing intent. Difficulty: inexpensive counts, careful predictor integration [6]. Compare popularity, last-item transitions, and recency-weighted pairwise scores.

**Selected idea: matched replacement probe.** Retain this diagnostic extension; use the behavioral ladder as a cheap companion. For each paired recent/older edit, use the same donor, preserving positions, padding, timestamps, and untouched items. Hold the last item fixed; analyze final-position replacement separately. Match donor-to-displaced-item difficulty using training popularity, smoothed transitions, and optional TF-IDF similarity. Prespecify tolerances; report residuals, coverage, reuse, and unmatched cases.

For five supplied users/category and five seeded draws, freeze the model and candidate eligibility. Report overlap and rank displacement both with donors included and on a common donor-excluded pool; track donor movement separately. Identity replacements audit correctness. Average draws within users, then categories equally; show individual effects and leave-one-user-out sensitivity, with exploratory uncertainty conditional on fixed matches [7,8]. Restore modes/RNG states and retain `DiagnosisProbe` and its return contract. Treat findings as sensitivity; select subsequent interventions solely through unchanged host macro validation HR@10. No recommendation gain is established.

idea.description: Strengthen the existing diagnostic adapter with same-donor, position-preserving replacements that compare recent and older history positions while explicitly measuring matching quality, donor self-recommendation, and dependence on the final item.
idea.motivation: Current deletions alter content and positions together. Independently selected replacement donors add another confound. Paired replacements using the same donor improve interpretability, while behavioral baselines test whether simple popularity or local associations explain apparent sequence dependence. These diagnostics cannot establish current user purpose, harmful recency bias, or causal lexical dependence.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and the metrics/metric_definitions return structure. Use view.model as the actual trained module and retain or adapt log2feats, predict_score, item_emb, user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Run in evaluation and inference modes; restore every module's training flag and Python, NumPy, CPU torch, and CUDA RNG states in a finally block. Use an isolated seeded RNG for probes.

Build statistics exclusively from each dataset's training histories and permitted titles/descriptions. Never consume unavailable ratings, categories, prices, stores, review text, hidden test files, or inferred simulator traits. Standard SASRec consumes IDs and positions: text similarity is a matching variable, not evidence that the model reads words. If examining text-associated effects, cross text similarity with behavioral similarity and report the result as an association with item identity. Do not interpret weak embedding alignment as proof of healthy representations or scale-dependent margins as calibrated ranking accuracy.

Predeclare five draw seeds, 0–4, and select five supplied panel users per category without replacements. For each user, use the original left-padded, truncated sequence. Define the final item as its latest nonpadding position; define earlier recent and older regions by dividing the remaining nonpadding positions into two contiguous halves, with any extra position assigned to the recent half. Skip users without both regions. Sample one position from each region per draw. Never move items, compact padding, or change timestamps. Keeping timestamps attached to positions creates synthetic item/time combinations; document this limitation. Final-position edits form a separate analysis and are not pooled with earlier-position contrasts.

Define item frequency f(j) from training interactions, P(j)=f(j)/sum_k f(k), adjacent transition counts n(i,j), and n(i)=sum_j n(i,j). Use P(j|i)=[n(i,j)+alpha*P(j)]/[n(i)+alpha] with alpha=10 fixed before inspecting diagnostic outcomes; retain raw counts as support indicators. Fit optional word TF-IDF on training-catalog titles/descriptions using lowercase unigrams/bigrams, min_df=2, max_features=50000, and L2 normalization. Missing text is missing, not zero semantic similarity.

Require a common donor outside padding and the user's complete original history. For both displaced items, require absolute log-popularity distance at most 0.5 training-catalog SD and absolute log-smoothed incoming-transition-probability distance at most 0.5 SD, using the same predecessor at each edited position; handle a missing predecessor as a separate stratum. Require the two donor-to-displaced-item TF-IDF cosines to differ by at most 0.1 when both are available. These are proposed operational defaults, not thresholds justified by Austin's propensity-score results. Choose uniformly among feasible donors using the draw RNG. Skip pairs without joint support rather than substituting different donors or relaxing calipers after inspecting effects. Report chosen positions, IDs, match distances, standardized balance differences where estimable, raw transition support, text availability, unmatched fractions, and donor reuse. Sparse overlap may substantially restrict conclusions.

For each user, keep C equal to the full catalog excluding the complete original training history across all edits. Also define C_minus by excluding every donor selected for that user's recorded edits from C. Recompute the unedited baseline separately on each pool; compare each edit only with its corresponding baseline. This prevents newly inserted or removed items from changing eligibility and provides a common donor-excluded audit. Score in chunks on one GPU, with deterministic item-ID tie breaking. Report top-10 overlap, mean absolute rank displacement of original top-10 items, strict pair-order reversals, absolute logit change, final-feature L2 change, donor score/rank movement on C, and recent-minus-older paired differences. Identity replacements and repeated inference must reproduce baseline scores and rankings within documented numerical tolerance. Preserve existing positive-rescaling checks where applicable.

Average draws within each user before equal category averaging and the four-category macro average. Report individual effects and leave-one-user-out sensitivity within categories. Optional percentile intervals use 2000 within-category user bootstrap draws conditional on fixed recorded matches, with seed 42. Label them exploratory: five users/category provide weak uncertainty estimates, repeated donors are not independent users, and these intervals exclude rematching, training-seed variability, and adaptive search. Do not bootstrap and rematch fixed-neighbor estimators without a justified procedure.

Keep the candidate-set disagreement audit and evidence-backed unresolved-case rubric as separate directions. Add low-cost training-only popularity, smoothed last-item transition, and recency-weighted pairwise scoring controls before expensive new architectures. An illustrative pairwise score is sum_t w_t*P(j|i_t), with normalized weights w_t proportional to 2^[-age(t)/10]; freeze this default before evaluation. Prefix shuffling with the last item fixed and last-item-only inference provide complementary controls but can introduce distribution shift. Their apparent success or low model sensitivity cannot prove the absence of higher-order learning.

Do not edit benchmark inputs or splits. Evaluate shortlisted trained interventions through the unchanged host evaluator using preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, evaluation seed 42, 200 validation users/category, and 99 unique negatives. Report per-category and equal-category macro HR@10, including paired changes only when the host exposes the necessary unchanged user-level outcomes. Training-only audit holdouts, if used, are auxiliary and must never replace or modify benchmark splits. No diagnostic becomes a surrogate selection objective. Avoid selecting calipers or interventions repeatedly on the twenty-user panel; log hypotheses and diagnostic cost, and cap donor search/scoring to respect the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. No training or improvement is claimed in this report.

Retain all four routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], single-GPU execution, and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Respect SASREC_EPOCHS=200 when provided by the environment. Diagnostic-only changes do not require architecture changes; any later architecture or inference change must update the predictor writer so working/predict.py loads the trained model consistently.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    save all module flags and global RNG states
    try:
        enter evaluation and inference modes
        build training-only frequency, transition, optional TF-IDF statistics
        for each dataset and its five supplied panel users:
            x = original padded training sequence
            C = catalog minus complete original training history
            plan = []
            for seed in [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]:
                choose one older and one recent nonfinal position
                find donors jointly satisfying declared calipers at both positions
                if no shared donor exists:
                    record unmatched pair; continue
                sample one shared donor using isolated seeded RNG
                record two separate replacements, match residuals, and support
            plan final-position edits separately
            C_minus = C minus all donors recorded for this user
            for pool in [C, C_minus]:
                baseline = score(x, pool, deterministic_ties=True)
                verify identity replacement and repeated-inference audits
                for planned paired edit:
                    score recent and older replacement separately on pool
                    record paired stability and original-top-10 rank changes
                score final-position edits as a separate stratum
            record donor score/rank changes on C
            average paired draws within this user
        aggregate equally within categories, then across four categories
        report individual effects, coverage, balance, failures, and cost
        report leave-one-user-out sensitivity
        optionally bootstrap users within categories with matches fixed
        label sensitivity, uncertainty limits, and missing evidence explicitly
        return metrics, metric_definitions
    finally:
        restore all module flags and global RNG states

Run cheap training-only behavioral controls as separate baselines.
Select subsequent trained interventions only with unchanged host macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Same-donor contrasts, final-item stratification, and common donor-excluded ranking pools strengthen the existing adapter in a useful combination.
originality.negative: Position-preserving substitutions, matched perturbations, and recency diagnostics already have precedents; this is a controlled diagnostic extension rather than a new recommender.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish several competing explanations for history sensitivity and motivate inexpensive, validation-tested model interventions.
future_potential.negative: Synthetic histories, restricted matching overlap, and the small exploratory panel may limit generalization; diagnostic changes may not predict HR@10 gains.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses existing scoring hooks, catalog ranking, panel selection, and architecture compatibility interfaces.
code_difficulty.negative: Joint donor matching, consistent candidate masks, donor-excluded baselines, deterministic ranking, and correct clustered summaries add substantial implementation work.

related_work.title: [1] Measuring Recency Bias
contributions: Introduces a recency diagnostic and reports improvements from reducing excessive recency bias.
limitations: Sensitivity alone does not establish harmful recency dependence, current purpose, or improvement on this benchmark.

related_work.title: [2] Positional Encoding Is Not the Same as Context
contributions: Distinguishes item-order information from temporal footprints in sequential recommendation.
limitations: Motivates positional controls but does not validate this matched replacement protocol or eliminate synthetic-history distribution shift.

related_work.title: [3] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with exact metrics and change model ordering.
limitations: Does not invalidate the prescribed benchmark; full-catalog diagnostics remain auxiliary and cannot replace host macro validation HR@10.

related_work.title: [4] Can LLM be a Personalized Judge?
contributions: Reports limited overall agreement with actual preferences and stronger agreement on high-certainty cases.
limitations: Does not supply preference labels or validate semantic judgments for these twenty training users; unresolved evidence must remain separate from rejection.

related_work.title: [5] ICMA
contributions: Provides a precedent for substituting related items at existing history positions while preserving sequence length and order.
limitations: Does not establish that paired same-donor substitutions identify recency mechanisms or improve the pinned RecHarness task.

related_work.title: [6] SASRec original implementation
contributions: Provides the item-ID and position-based sequential recommendation implementation underlying the baseline.
Clarifies why changing titles alone cannot change predictions in an ID-only model.
limitations: Item-ID substitutions change learned representations and behavioral associations together; title matching cannot identify causal lexical dependence.

related_work.title: [7] A Practitioner's Guide to Cluster-Robust Inference
contributions: Explains dependence within clusters and difficulties with inference when the number of clusters is small.
limitations: Does not validate conventional confidence intervals for five users per category or remove adaptive-search and matching uncertainty.

related_work.title: [8] On the Failure of the Bootstrap for Matching Estimators
contributions: Demonstrates settings in which ordinary bootstrap inference fails for nearest-neighbor matching estimators.
limitations: Does not imply every bootstrap of fixed diagnostic user summaries fails; conditional summaries and rematched estimators require different interpretations.

related_work.title: [9] Optimal Caliper Widths for Propensity-Score Matching
contributions: Studies caliper choices for specified propensity-score treatment-effect estimation settings.
limitations: Its 0.2-SD recommendation is not a universal threshold for text similarity, popularity, or transition-probability matching.
